questions.question: Which entries are suppressed by the causal mask in `MiniGPT.forward` for a sequence of length 4?
options: Scores from a position to every earlier key.
Only the diagonal score at each position.
Scores from a position to later keys.
All scores in the final transformer block.
questions.explanation: `np.triu(-1e9, k=1)` fills positions above the diagonal, preventing token position i from attending to future positions j > i.

questions.question: For `embed_dim=768` and `num_heads=12`, what is the per-head dimension in `MultiHeadAttention`?
questions.explanation: The implementation asserts divisibility and sets `head_dim = embed_dim // num_heads`, giving 768 // 12 = 64.

questions.question: What shape does `MiniGPT.forward` return for inputs shaped `(batch, seq)` and vocabulary size `V`?
options: `(batch, seq, V)` logits.
`(seq, batch, V)` probabilities.
`(batch, V)` one pooled vector.
`(V, seq, batch)` token IDs.
questions.explanation: The tied output head multiplies every final hidden state by the embedding transpose, producing one logit vector of length V per batch position.

questions.question: Why does the training demo use `tokens[:-1]` as inputs and `tokens[1:]` as targets?
options: To hide all padding from the model.
Each position learns to predict the next token.
To make the vocabulary one item smaller.
To turn a causal mask into bidirectional attention.
questions.explanation: Shifting the target sequence by one aligns the hidden state after the prefix with the token that should come next.

questions.question: If the same next-token logits are divided by a temperature below 1 in `generate`, what qualitative change should sampling show?
options: A uniform distribution independent of the logits.
A reversal that makes the lowest logit most likely.
Lower temperature sharpens the distribution.
No change, because temperature is applied after sampling.
questions.explanation: Dividing logits by a value below 1 increases their spread before softmax, concentrating probability on the larger logits.

questions.question: Which sequence matches the pre-LN residual structure of `TransformerBlock.forward`?
options: FFN(LN(Attention(LN(x)))) with no skip paths.
LN(x + Attention(x)) followed by a second normalization only.
Attention(x) + FFN(x), then one final residual add.
`x + Attention(LN(x))`, then add `FFN(LN(updated_x))`.
questions.explanation: The block first adds attention applied to normalized x, then adds the feed-forward result applied to the normalized intermediate state.
